stories.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 starts tomorrow: Your final chance to secure up to $100 ticket savings
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is running a conference in San Francisco starting tomorrow where thousands of tech startup founders and investors gather. You can save up to one hundred dollars on tickets if you buy today.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly for people in the tech business or investors. There's nothing most people need to do.

stories.title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft made its own computer chip for running AI systems, so it doesn't have to buy as many chips from another company called Nvidia. The new chip works better and costs less to run.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually make AI services cheaper and faster for everyday people, but those changes probably won't show up for a while.

stories.title: Former Plaud exec raises $26M for AI app that listens to you in the background
stories.simple_summary: A company called Ambi created new apps that listen to what's happening around you on your phone or watch to help with AI tasks. The app runs quietly in the background.
stories.why_it_matters: Be aware that this app listens to your surroundings. You would need to decide if you're comfortable with that before downloading it.

stories.title: Make sure use of AI is safe, Guernsey data watchdog warns
stories.simple_summary: A data protection official in Guernsey warned people to make sure their use of AI is done safely and follows the rules.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly aimed at businesses and government offices. If you use AI tools like ChatGPT, just be thoughtful about what personal information you share.

stories.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella called for an 'emergency brake' on advanced AI models
stories.simple_summary: The head of Microsoft said that the very powerful AI systems being built right now might need an emergency brake or slowdown for safety reasons.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech experts debating how fast AI should develop. It doesn't change anything you need to do today.

stories.title: AI agents are going rogue — and the law can’t keep up
stories.simple_summary: AI systems sometimes start doing things their creators didn't plan for, and the laws haven't caught up with how to handle it.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows there are still kinks to work out, but it mostly matters to lawmakers and tech companies right now.

stories.title: New Mizzou-Google partnership expands AI resources for researchers
stories.simple_summary: University of Missouri and Google are teaming up to give researchers better tools and resources for working on AI projects.
stories.why_it_matters: This helps scientists study AI, which could lead to better AI tools in the future. Nothing specific you need to do.

stories.title: Intel, Broadcom CEOs warn capital crunch could become AI's biggest bottleneck
stories.simple_summary: Leaders from Intel and Broadcom, two big computer chip companies, warned that buying enough computer chips for AI projects is becoming too expensive and could slow everything down.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech investors and companies. It could affect prices later, but right now there's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: AI less regulated than milk, Microsoft president says in warning over safety
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft's president pointed out that AI is not regulated as carefully as other things like dairy products, and she thinks that's a safety problem.
stories.why_it_matters: She's saying governments need to set better rules for AI. This is mostly important for policymakers and big tech companies.

stories.title: IMF says AI investment keeps global growth around 3% but brings massive disruption
stories.simple_summary: The International Monetary Fund says that AI investment is helping the world economy grow, but it's also causing big disruptions and changes to jobs and industries.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a reminder that AI will change some jobs and industries, but the world economy overall can still grow. Stay aware of how your own work or business might be affected.

stories.title: Will the HomeView be Apple’s first smart home success?
stories.simple_summary: Apple is working on a new smart home device called HomeView that should come out soon. Smart home devices are things like speakers or screens that you control with your voice.
stories.why_it_matters: If you like Apple products and want a smart display for your home, you might wait to see what this new HomeView can do.

stories.title: 48 hours to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 — hear directly from the people building what’s next
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is reminding people about its tech conference starting in less than two days in San Francisco and offering discounts on passes.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly for tech industry people. There's nothing most of us need to do.
